title: Elasticity knee calculator — INT8/FP8/4-bit tradeoff notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick working doc for an experimental ‘elasticity knee’ calculator that estimates where diminishing quality returns (and rising latency/cost) make further precision reductions unattractive. Goal: give product + solutions an actionable single-line recommendation (e.g., prefer FP8 until query-length > 1024 then switch to INT8) plus confidence bands.

Background / motivation:
- Lots of existing sheets enumerate cost vs accuracy per-bitwidth but they lack an explicit notion of elasticity: how much accuracy do you lose per unit cost saved as you step from FP16 -> FP8 -> INT8 -> 4-bit?
- For customers the decision surface is three-dimensional (cost, latency, quality). We need a compact heuristic that:
  1) flags the ‘knee’ where incremental cost savings yield outsized quality drop;
  2) surfaces recommended fallback thresholds for model length, top-p or beam settings, and batching;
  3) produces a single recommended profile per workload: conservative / balanced / aggressive.

Definitions used here (working):
- Baseline precision: FP16 (or float32 where relevant). Quality_baseline = reference metric (e.g., exact-match F1 or BLEU depending on eval).
- Precision variants: FP8, INT8, 4-bit (quantized llm weights + adapted activation/kv handling).
- Elasticity (E): percent delta quality / percent delta cost when moving from A -> B. Expressed as E(A->B) = (Q_B - Q_A) / (C_B - C_A) where Q = normalized quality (0..1), C = normalized per-token cost ($). Negative E indicates quality drop per dollar saved.
- Knee: the point at which second derivative of quality w.r.t cost exceeds a threshold (intuitively where d^2Q/dC^2 becomes strongly negative). Implementation: estimate discrete curvature across bitwidths and pick highest curvature magnitude subject to sample size.

Inputs to the calculator (min set):
- Model family and baseline size (e.g., Llama2-13B, Mistral-7B)
- Baseline quality metric & eval set (single numeric)
- Measured latency per-token at baseline for target hardware (ms/token) and per-bitwidth measurements if available
- Cost per-hour of serving instance (or effective per-token cost derived from throughput)
- Batch size baseline and target distribution (p50/p95 seq lengths)
- Quantization method (GPTQ, AWQ, LLM-QAT) and notes on KV-cache fidelity
- Tolerance thresholds: acceptable quality loss (absolute %), latency SLO (ms), unit-cost target ($/1k tokens)

Simple internal formulas used in the sheet: (these are plain approximations; we show how to parameterize)
- C_per_token(precision) = base_infra_cost / throughput(precision)  # throughput measured in tokens/sec for the model on target node
- Q_norm(precision) = (eval_metric_precision / eval_metric_baseline)  # normalize to baseline=1.0
- E(A->B) = (Q_norm_B - Q_norm_A) / (C_per_token_B - C_per_token_A)
- Knee score across sequence {A,B,C} = |(Q_B - Q_A) - (Q_C - Q_B)| / max(epsilon, |C_B - C_A| + |C_C - C_B|)  # rough discrete curvature

Heuristic recommendation rules (prototype):
1) If median E(A->B) > -0.02 (i.e., <2% quality loss per 10% cost saved) prefer lower precision for cost-sensitive workloads.
2) If knee score highest at step (B->C) and absolute Q_drop from baseline > tolerance, mark knee there and recommend stopping before C.
3) If latency_delta(precision) > SLO_margin -> reject precision for latency-sensitive routes.
4) For mixed workloads (long-tail seq lengths), bias towards conservative profiles unless cold-start cost dominates.

Example scenarios (toy numbers, show sheet-like output):
- Baseline: Llama2-13B FP16: Q=0.86 (rouge), throughput=1200 tok/s, cost_token=$0.0010
- FP8: Q=0.845, throughput=1700 tok/s, cost_token=$0.00071
- INT8: Q=0.81, throughput=2100 tok/s, cost_token=$0.00057
- 4-bit: Q=0.74, throughput=2500 tok/s, cost_token=$0.00048

Compute: (normalized to FP16=1.0 quality)
- Q_norm: FP16=1.00, FP8=0.983, INT8=0.942, 4bit=0.860
- Cost per token: FP16=1.00 (norm), FP8=0.71, INT8=0.57, 4bit=0.48
- E(FP16->FP8) = (0.983-1.00)/(0.71-1.00) = (-0.017)/(-0.29) = 0.058 (positive because both numerator and denominator negative) -> small quality loss per cost saved
- E(FP8->INT8) = (0.942-0.983)/(0.57-0.71) = (-0.041)/(-0.14) = 0.293 -> much larger elasticity (bigger quality drop per dollar saved)
- E(INT8->4bit) = (0.860-0.942)/(0.48-0.57) = (-0.082)/(-0.09) = 0.911 -> extremely high (avoid)

Interpretation: the ‘knee’ is between INT8->4bit; but step FP8->INT8 already shows increased penalty. Recommendation: Balanced profile = FP8 for most routes; Aggressive only for low-stakes high-throughput batch jobs may take INT8 if latency and cost priority, but avoid 4-bit for QA/eval-critical routes.

Unresolved/notes-to-self (TODOs):
- Add sensitivity to prompt-template (prefix length) — quality drop often worse for long-context prefix-heavy tasks.
- Integrate KV-cache degradation multiplier (we have observations that INT8 + cheap KV-approx yields >1.5x quality loss on chat-history tasks).
- Replace toy curvature function with small regression fit across continuous quantization curves (if we can generate sliced fidelity metrics via progressive rounding).
- Add Monte Carlo sim for workload mix (p50/p90/p99 seq lengths) to produce expected cost and p95 latency.
- Add export mode: convert recommendation into Redwood Optimize JSON config used by the optimizer service (see linked PR #218).

Practical checklist for solutions / field engineers when recommending:
- Ask for exact eval set and run baseline eval on the same infra node we will use for serving (disk layout + CUDA version matter).
- Provide single-number recommendation + confidence: e.g., "FP8 (recommended, medium confidence) — expect 12–18% cost savings, <2% quality drop vs FP16 on provided eval; INT8 only if >95% cost cut required and customer accepts up to 6% quality loss."
- Snapshot: include p50/p95 latency at the chosen batch sizes and a fallback policy: FP8 -> INT8 -> FP16 with automatic rollback if eval drift > X.

Appendix: short logging of an A/B experiment run Nov 2025 (raw notes)
- Setup: Llama2-13B, responses truncated at 512 tokens, batch=8 on A100-80GB
- Observed: FP8 throughput +42% vs FP16, INT8 +75%, 4-bit +108%
- Eval (n=2k Q/A): FP8 -1.7% absolute, INT8 -5.0% absolute, 4-bit -12.0% absolute
- Latency p95: FP16=210ms, FP8=165ms, INT8=120ms, 4-bit=98ms
- Note: INT8 regressed badly on arithmetic-style prompts; flagged to SRE for a targeted micro-benchmark.

Questions for next sync:
- Do we want this heuristic surfaced in Console as a per-route suggestion (yes/no)?
- If yes, what guardrails for auto-switching between precisions should we enforce? (cool-down window, rollouts, eval triggers)
- Which customers should we pilot with first? suggested: fintech partner (non-production sandbox), e-commerce search cluster (batch inference).
